sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- WSJ, unnamed US officials] With the midterms over, Trump's advisers are split: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper support a return to major combat operations; VP JD Vance and envoy Steve Witkoff seek continued diplomacy to end the war and reopen Hormuz; Secretary of State Rubio and Treasury Secretary Bessent advocate tightening sanctions + continuing the blockade; Netanyahu is still pushing for renewed strikes; Gulf allies are more skeptical. [VERIFIED FACT -- Trump, Oval Office, Thu Nov 5] 'Now we will make a decision... I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I will have to. You'll know soon enough.' [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- WSJ] Qatar launched an 11th-hour attempt to stave off a new US operation; Emir Tamim spoke with Trump Friday; Iranian officials are set to return to Doha in the coming days, possibly as early as Saturday; the deal under discussion would shrink preliminary-talks timetable from 60 days (June MoU term) to 2 days. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- WSJ] Ideal timeframe to resume operations begins later this month when additional equipment arrives; USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group is in Singapore for a port call from Friday and is not expected in the Middle East for at least another two weeks; an additional Marine expeditionary unit joins ~20 ships already in the region later this month; a Patriot system has been moved to Israel. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- WSJ] Hegseth/Cooper advised that resuming attacks -- targeting Iranian energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities and missile/drone arsenals -- is the only way to make Iran surrender its nuclear material. [CORROBORATING CONTEXT -- Bloomberg via Ynet, Nov 6] Tehran is showing new flexibility over its nuclear programme; US and Iran are moving closer to a possible diplomatic breakthrough. [CORROBORATING CONTEXT -- Axios via Times Now/HUM, Nov 6] Trump met his national security team Thu Nov 5, first Iran meeting since the midterms; CENTCOM is finalising preparations to restart major combat operations but has no fresh directive.
sections.what_verified: 4 distinct declared-tier families, but the WSJ's distinctive claims (the internal split, the named camps, the 60-to-2-day timetable, the Roosevelt/Marine timelines) rest on ONE origin -- WSJ's unnamed US officials. Surrounding facts are independently corroborated: Trump decision-pending + 'You'll know soon enough' (Trump on record, multiple families); Qatar mediation + Doha return (Qatar IMO statement, recorded 0400-04; Gulf News T3); CENTCOM preparation without orders (Axios T2); Tehran nuclear flexibility (Bloomberg T1 via Ynet). The internal-split reporting itself is single-origin and unconfirmed by any on-record source.
sections.what_disputed: A White House official told WSJ Trump is 'in no hurry' to decide as the Iranian economy sputters and oil flows through Hormuz. Some experts (Ben Taleblu, FDD) say it is unclear additional strikes will force a deal after the regime survived eight months of war; Gregory Brew (Eurasia Group) says maintaining sanctions + blockade is the path of least resistance but means continuing the war indefinitely. Iran is threatening to expand retaliation beyond the Middle East if attacked. No on-record confirmation of the Hegseth/Cooper vs Vance/Witkoff split from any named official.
sections.why_matters: Trump's own team is split in two -- the hawks want to finish the job, his VP wants the deal -- and he decides now. Hard numbers: Roosevelt 2 weeks out, ~20 US ships already in the region, 60 days of talks squeezed to 2. Claim-busting frame: the deal would reopen Hormuz; the war camp wants Iran's energy, nuclear and missile sites hit.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (WSJ published Nov 7, crawled 04:18Z = 08:18 ; zero 'clashing advisers'/'Hegseth and Cooper'/'60 days to two days' mentions in any prior Nov 6/7 scan -- grep confirms) -- Trump's advisers split over the Iran war decision: Hegseth + CENTCOM chief Cooper push a return to major combat operations, Vance + Witkoff push diplomacy, Netanyahu pushes renewed strikes; Qatar's 11th-hour mediation; Iranian officials due back in Doha possibly Saturday; USS Theodore Roosevelt ~2 weeks out

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump's own team is split in two -- the hawks want to finish the job, his VP wants the deal -- and he decides now. Hard numbers: Roosevelt 2 weeks out, ~20 US ships already in the region, 60 days of talks squeezed to 2. Claim-busting frame: the deal would reopen Hormuz; the war camp wants Iran's energy, nuclear and missile sites hit. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Finish the job or take the deal? Hegseth and Cooper want major combat operations to force Iran to surrender its nuclear material; Vance and Witkoff want the two-day deal that reopens Hormuz. After the midterm rebuke, is the war the price of a legacy -- or the thing that cost Trump Congress?
